items.name: analyst
items.description: Insect caste that turns data into checked numbers and clear conclusions for one task card at a time. Use for data and business analysis, KPIs and metrics, cohort and segment analysis, A/B test reads, financial models, forecasts, budgets and variance analysis, and data cleaning or profiling.

items.name: coder
items.description: Insect caste that writes and changes code for one task card at a time. Use for implementing features, fixing bugs, fixing broken builds and small refactors, in frontend or backend code.

items.name: designer
items.description: Insect caste that does UI and UX design for one task card at a time. Use for setting a design direction, design tokens and component specs, screen and state design, prototypes, heuristic usability and accessibility reviews, and checking rendered UI against the design.

items.name: documenter
items.description: Insect caste that writes and updates technical documentation for one task card at a time. Use for READMEs, API references, setup and how-to guides, tutorials, migration notes, architecture overviews and keeping docs in sync with code changes.

items.name: foreman
items.description: Manager that keeps the taskboard flowing. Its code reflexes handle claims, leases, dependency unlocks, retries and insect scaling instantly; its brain wakes only for stuck, oversized or deadlocked cards and periodic board reviews. Use to run the board; never for planning goals or doing card work.

items.name: inspector
items.description: Quality manager that checks every finished card against its acceptance criteria, with fresh evidence, before it can be marked done; also runs the final whole-goal check. Read-only. Use when a card reaches review or the Queen closes a goal.

items.name: librarian
items.description: Memory manager that keeps the Brain and the skill catalog healthy. Code reflexes dedupe, rank, decay, check freshness and score health; its brain consolidates memories, prepares conflicts and fact confirmations for the user, runs audits, distills lessons and proposes new or retired skills. Use for Brain upkeep and catalog changes.

items.name: queen
items.description: The hive's orchestrator and its only voice to the user. Turns a user goal into waves of task cards on the taskboard, gets big plans approved, rules on conflicts, assembles verified results and reports back. Use for every user goal; never for doing task work itself.

items.name: researcher
items.description: Insect caste that answers one research question per task card with cited, confidence-rated findings. Use for software research (existing libraries, tools, prior art before building) and general research (topics, markets, competitors, trends, literature reviews, due diligence).

items.name: reviewer
items.description: Insect caste that reviews code changes for one task card at a time, read-only. Use for correctness, security, maintainability, performance and test-coverage review of a diff, branch or file before work is marked done.

items.name: scout
items.description: Read-only explorer manager that surveys a codebase or topic before the Queen plans, and answers "where is X / how does Y work" questions with cited locations. Looks, never touches; reports risks and opportunities but decides nothing. Use when the area is unfamiliar or a direct search failed; skip when the exact file or symbol is already known.

items.name: tester
items.description: Insect caste that writes and runs tests for one task card at a time. Use for unit, integration, API and end-to-end tests, coverage gaps, reproducing bugs as failing tests, and diagnosing flaky tests.

items.name: treasurer
items.description: Budget and routing manager. Its code reflexes meter tokens and cost, enforce budgets and rate limits, and route every card to a model and effort level (the model + effort router). Its brain wakes to tune routing from outcomes, explain unusual spend and estimate plan costs. Use for anything about spend, limits or model choice.

items.name: watchdog
items.description: Health manager that detects loops, crashes, stalls and overspending agents and runs the breaker ladder (steer, then constrain, then stop). Its reflexes are code and react in milliseconds; its brain wakes only to diagnose unclear or repeated incidents. Use to guard agent health; never to do or judge task work.

items.name: writer
items.description: Insect caste that drafts non-code text for one task card at a time. Use for emails and email sequences, social posts, blog articles, landing-page and marketing copy, newsletters, announcements, scripts, and SEO briefs or on-page optimization. Drafts only; never sends or publishes.

items.name: accessibility
items.description: Build and audit UI to WCAG 2.2 Level AA - semantic HTML first, correct names/roles/states, keyboard and focus management, forms and errors, contrast, target size, reflow, motion and live regions - verified by automated scans plus manual keyboard and screen-reader checks. Use when building or reviewing components or pages, fixing a11y findings, or when a card mentions WCAG, a11y or screen readers.

items.name: api-design
items.description: HTTP/REST API contract design - resource naming, method semantics, status codes, error bodies (RFC 9457 problem details), pagination, filtering and sorting, versioning and deprecation, idempotency keys, conditional requests, long-running operations, rate-limit signals and a pre-ship checklist. Use when designing, changing or reviewing HTTP endpoints or an OpenAPI spec.

items.name: backend-patterns
items.description: Node.js/TypeScript server structure - handler/service/repository layers, edge validation, typed errors and a central handler, auth boundaries, data access (N+1, transactions, pooling), caching, durable jobs, outbound timeouts and retries, logging and graceful shutdown. Use when building or reviewing server code, API handlers or workers in Node/TypeScript.

items.name: brainstorming
items.description: Finds out what the user actually wants, and why, then turns it into an approved design doc with the chosen approach. Use before planning or building anything new or changing behavior (software or not) when something that would change the result is missing from the request. Mainly for the Queen; other castes use it for design questions inside their own card.

items.name: browser-automation
items.description: Drive a web browser reliably and cheaply with the snapshot-and-ref loop - open, snapshot, act on element refs, wait for the expected change, re-snapshot. Covers reading pages, forms, waits, tabs, data extraction, troubleshooting and safety. Use for any task card that needs a real browser; agent-browser CLI is the primary tool.

items.name: build-error-resolution
items.description: Get a failing build, type check, compile, dependency install or framework startup back to green with the smallest possible changes - no refactoring, no redesign, no silencing checks. Use when a build, type check or startup fails. Language specifics for TypeScript/React and Python/Django are in references.

items.name: code-review
items.description: Review a code change for real problems only (correctness, security, maintainability, performance, tests), filtered by confidence, no style nitpicks, reported one line per finding as `path:line: severity: problem. fix.` with a clear verdict. Use when reviewing a diff, branch or card result, and when requesting a review of your own finished work.'

items.name: coding-discipline
items.description: Baseline rules for writing and changing any code - think before coding, keep it simple, change only what the task needs, and define how success will be verified. Includes language-neutral quality rules (naming, errors, nesting, constants, comments). Load for every coding task, review or refactor, in any language.

items.name: compact-output
items.description: Write agent-to-agent messages, task results, handoffs and logs in a compact style at one of three levels (lite, terse, ultra) that cuts filler but keeps every fact, path, number, code span and error verbatim. Use for anything another agent or the Brain reads. Never for text the user reads.

items.name: deep-research
items.description: Answer a question from many sources with a cited report: check the Brain first, split the topic into sub-questions, search and fully read key sources, weigh conflicting evidence, and mark confidence and gaps. Use for in-depth research, technology evaluation, competitive or market analysis, and due diligence. For a quick check before building, use search-first."

items.name: deployment-patterns
items.description: Vendor-neutral release practice. CI/CD stages, build-once artefacts, environments, rolling/blue-green/canary rollouts, liveness and readiness checks, config and secrets via environment, backward-compatible migrations, rollbacks and production readiness. Use when setting up or changing a pipeline, planning a release, or checking production readiness. Production deploys need user approval.

items.name: dispatching-parallel-work
items.description: Decides which task cards are truly independent so they can be released to the taskboard at the same time, and which must wait, be merged or be serialized. Use when the Queen posts a wave of 2+ cards, or the Foreman balances the board, re-releases cards or decides how many insects to run at once.

items.name: django-patterns
items.description: Build and review Django and Django REST Framework apps securely. Covers settings layout, models and DB constraints, migrations, custom QuerySets, N+1 prevention, service layer with transactions, serializers and viewsets, caching, signals, middleware and a production security checklist. Use when working on any Django or DRF code, migrations, permissions or deployment settings.

items.name: docker-patterns
items.description: Write and review Dockerfiles and Compose files. Covers multi-stage builds, layer caching, pinned minimal base images, non-root read-only containers, build and runtime secrets, networks, volumes, healthchecks, local dev stacks and isolated throwaway test containers. Use when creating, changing or debugging container images or Compose setups. For releasing to environments, load deployment-patterns.

items.name: e2e-testing
items.description: Write, run and maintain end-to-end browser tests for critical user journeys - risk-based journey selection, stable user-facing selectors, condition-based waits, isolated test data, artifacts on failure, and flaky-test detection and quarantine. Playwright Test by default. Use when adding or fixing E2E tests, triaging flaky runs, or wiring E2E into CI.

items.name: error-handling
items.description: Language-neutral error handling. Classifying failures, where to catch, typed errors, propagating with context, API error responses, logging once, user vs developer messages, timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breakers and fallbacks. Use when designing error types, adding try/catch, retries or fallbacks, mapping errors to HTTP responses, or reviewing code for silent failures.

items.name: executing-a-task-card
items.description: Takes one claimed task card from its Brain brief to a verified result and a handoff, staying inside the card's scope and escalating instead of guessing. Use whenever an insect starts or resumes work on a taskboard card, of any caste.

items.name: fastapi-patterns
items.description: Build and review FastAPI services. Covers project layout, app factory and lifespan, pydantic-settings config, Pydantic v2 schemas, Annotated dependencies, thin routers over a service layer, async database sessions, auth (401 vs 403), error handlers and tests with httpx and dependency overrides. Use when creating or changing FastAPI endpoints, schemas, dependencies or their tests.

items.name: frontend-patterns
items.description: Framework-neutral frontend architecture decisions - where state lives, server-state fetching and caching, loading/error/empty states, forms and validation, routing and URL state, styling approach, code splitting, client-side security. Use when planning, building or reviewing UI architecture in any framework. For React component and hook rules, load react-patterns instead.

items.name: git-workflow
items.description: Version control for one task card - work in an isolated branch or worktree, write compact Conventional Commits, keep history clean, resolve conflicts, and finish the branch (merge locally, open a pull request, or keep). Pushing to shared repos and deleting branches or work need approval. Use whenever a task changes files in a git repository.

items.name: lean-build
items.description: Build new behaviour as one complete, narrow, end-to-end slice that fits the existing system, with explicit non-goals and a clear stop condition. Use for new features, product slices or integrations where overbuilding is a risk. Not for bug fixes (surgical-patch) or restructuring (safe-refactor).

items.name: memory-compression
items.description: Shrink long natural-language memory (Brain summaries, agent notes, boot cards, instruction files, todo lists) into a compact form that keeps every fact, heading, code span, path and number, while the readable original is kept as its own version. Use when a memory item is loaded often or exceeds its token budget. Not for code or config files.

items.name: postgres-patterns
items.description: PostgreSQL schema design, data types, indexing, query patterns (upsert, keyset pagination, job queues), safe online migrations, connection pooling, timeouts, roles and row-level security, and reading query plans. Use when designing tables or indexes, writing SQL or migrations for Postgres, adding RLS policies, or when a Postgres query is slow.

items.name: python-patterns
items.description: Idiomatic, typed, maintainable Python. Covers readability rules, type hints, exceptions, context managers, generators, dataclasses, choosing a concurrency model, project layout and tooling. Use when writing, refactoring or reviewing Python code. For tests load python-testing; for FastAPI or Django load those skills.

items.name: python-review
items.description: Python review checks on top of code-review: injection and unsafe APIs, error handling, type hints, mutable defaults, concurrency and async pitfalls, plus FastAPI (async, dependencies, Pydantic models, CORS) and Django (ORM, migrations, DRF, settings) sections. Use when a diff touches .py files, migrations or Python project config.'

items.name: python-testing
items.description: Write and review pytest tests for Python. Covers test structure, fixtures and scopes, parametrize, mocking only at real boundaries, async tests, temp files, markers, database isolation and coverage. Use when writing, fixing or reviewing Python tests, or setting up pytest config. Pair with test-driven-development for the red-green-refactor cycle.

items.name: react-patterns
items.description: Idiomatic React 18/19 component design - pure render and derived state, hooks discipline, where state should live, composition instead of boolean props (compound components, explicit variants, provider-injected state), server/client component boundaries, Suspense and error boundaries, forms and actions. Use when writing, reviewing or refactoring React components, hooks or component APIs.

items.name: react-performance
items.description: Impact-ordered performance rules for React and Next.js-style apps - async waterfalls, bundle size, server caching and server/client serialization, client fetch dedup, re-renders, rendering and hydration, JS hot paths. Use when writing or reviewing React code for speed, or diagnosing slow loads, slow interactions, large bundles or Core Web Vitals regressions.

items.name: react-testing
items.description: Behavior-first tests for React components and hooks with Testing Library, Vitest or Jest, user-event, network-level mocking (MSW) and axe accessibility checks, plus when to move to real-browser component tests or end-to-end tests. Use when writing, fixing or reviewing tests for React components, hooks, forms or pages, or setting up a React test stack.

items.name: receiving-review-feedback
items.description: Handle review findings with technical rigor: read all of it, clarify anything unclear before changing code, verify each item against the codebase, push back with evidence when it is wrong, then fix one item at a time and test each. Use when a reviewer, the Inspector or the Queen returns findings on your card, before implementing any suggestion.'

items.name: reversible-migration
items.description: Move a schema, data set, API, protocol, configuration or dependency from old to new safely - expand, migrate, verify, then contract - with a rollback path, no data loss and old and new versions working side by side. Use for any migration that existing data, readers or deployed clients depend on, including zero-downtime database changes.

items.name: safe-refactor
items.description: Restructure code without changing behaviour - extract, move, consolidate duplicates or remove dead code - with verification before and after every step. Use when a task asks for cleanup or restructuring. Not during active feature work in the same area, right before a release, or on code without tests you can trust.

items.name: search-first
items.description: Before building, look for what already exists: prior decisions, outcomes and open tasks in the Brain, code in the repo, skills and tools in the library, packages, and public projects. Then adopt, extend, compose or build. Use when starting a feature, adding a dependency or integration, or about to write a helper that may already exist."

items.name: security-review
items.description: OWASP-style security review of code and configuration: secrets, injection, XSS, access control, authentication, sensitive data, SSRF, unsafe deserialization, dependencies and infrastructure. Use when a change touches user input, auth, API endpoints, file uploads, payments, webhooks, crypto, secrets or sensitive data, when dependencies change, and before any release.'

items.name: surgical-patch
items.description: Fix a bug or make a small behaviour change at the narrowest layer that owns the wrong behaviour, with regression proof and nothing else touched. Use for bug fixes and small tweaks where preserving surrounding behaviour matters. Not for new features (use lean-build) or restructuring (use safe-refactor).

items.name: systematic-debugging
items.description: Find the root cause before changing anything: read the error, reproduce, gather evidence, rank hypotheses, test one at a time, then fix at the source with a failing test first. Use for any bug, test failure, build failure, flaky or intermittent behavior, performance regression or unexpected result, before proposing or editing a fix.'

items.name: task-handoff
items.description: Writes the short "done / where I left off / next step / blockers" checkpoint that lets the next agent resume a card in about 200 tokens, and reads a Brain task brief or handoff correctly before starting. Use when starting or resuming a card, before a session ends or its context is compacted, when blocked or escalating, and when finishing a card.

items.name: technical-writing
items.description: Write, edit and maintain developer docs (READMEs, guides, tutorials, API and config references, troubleshooting, migration notes, codemaps) that are verified against the code and kept in sync with it. Use after new features, API, dependency, setup or architecture changes, and when auditing docs for staleness. For a pure style review, use writing-guidelines.

items.name: test-driven-development
items.description: Write a failing test first, watch it fail for the right reason, make it pass with the smallest change, then refactor with the suite green. Use whenever a card adds or changes behavior (feature, bug fix, refactor, endpoint, component), before writing any implementation code, or when a card asks for red-green-refactor or a coverage target.

items.name: typescript-patterns
items.description: Write and review strict, type-safe TypeScript - compiler strictness, unknown over any, discriminated unions, brands, generics, validation at I/O boundaries, Result types, async concurrency and cancellation, module boundaries and type tests. Use when writing, reviewing or refactoring .ts/.tsx/.js code, designing types or tsconfig, or untangling cascading type errors.

items.name: typescript-review
items.description: TypeScript and JavaScript review checks on top of code-review: type safety, async correctness, error handling, Node.js pitfalls, injection sinks, plus a React section for hooks, rendering, server/client boundaries, accessibility and React-specific security. Use when a diff touches .ts, .tsx, .js, .jsx, .mjs or .cjs files.'

items.name: using-the-brain
items.description: Reads the shared Brain in tiers (boot card, index, detail, source file) within a token budget, and writes updates, outcomes, facts and decision proposals at the right trust level, deduped and free of secrets. Use at the start of any task, before reading raw files or chat history, and whenever you finish something worth remembering. Every agent.

items.name: verification-before-completion
items.description: Evidence before any "done", "fixed" or "passing" claim. Turn the card's acceptance criteria into the smallest set of checks that proves them, run them fresh, read the output, and report exactly pass, fail, unavailable or blocked. Use as every insect's last step before submitting a card, and as the Inspector's method for checking finished work.

items.name: web-app-qa
items.description: Systematic exploratory testing of a running web app in a real browser - smoke checks, feature-by-feature exploration, responsive and accessibility passes - with reproducible evidence for every finding (repro steps, screenshots, video, severity) and a ship verdict. Use to QA, dogfood or bug-hunt a site, or to verify a deployed feature on local, preview or staging.

items.name: web-design-guidelines
items.description: Set a product-specific design direction before building web UI, then build and review against concrete interface rules - interactions, forms, content states, typography, layout, motion, theming, performance - with a rendered finish check and terse file:line findings. Use when building, polishing or reviewing any web page, app screen, dashboard or component.

items.name: writing-guidelines
items.description: Review docs and other prose against general writing rules (planning, voice, banned filler and hype words, sentence patterns, headings, lists, code samples, numbers and units, typography, links, accountability) and report findings as file:line lines with a fix. Use when asked to review docs, check writing style, audit prose, or check voice and tone.
